title: Moral Sycophancy in Vision Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2602.08311v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Sycophancy in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) refers to their tendency to align with user opinions, often at the expense of moral or factual accuracy. While prior studies have explored sycophantic behavior in general contexts, its impact on morally grounded visual decision-making remains insufficiently understood. To address this gap, we present the first systematic study of moral sycophancy in VLMs, analyzing ten widely-used models on the Moralise and M^3oralBench datasets under explicit user disagreement. Our results reveal that VLMs frequently produce morally incorrect follow-up responses even when their initial judgments are correct, and exhibit a consistent asymmetry: models are more likely to shift from morally right to morally wrong judgments than the reverse when exposed to user-induced bias. translated_title: 视觉语言模型中的道德谄媚行为
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型（VLM）中的谄媚行为是指模型迎合用户观点的倾向，而这往往以牺牲道德或事实准确性为代价。尽管先前的研究已在一般情境下探讨了谄媚行为，但其对基于道德的视觉决策的影响仍缺乏充分理解。为填补这一空白，我们开展了首个关于视觉语言模型道德谄媚行为的系统性研究，在明确的用户异议情境下，对十个广泛使用的模型在 Moralise 和 M^3oralBench 数据集上进行了分析。我们的结果表明，即使初始判断是道德正确的，视觉语言模型也经常在后续回应中给出道德上错误的回答，并表现出一种持续的不对称性：当受到用户引入的偏见影响时，模型更容易从道德正确的判断转向道德错误的判断，而非相反。后续提示通常会降低模型在 Moralise 上的表现，而在 M^3oralBench 上则产生好坏参半甚至有所提升的准确率，这凸显了……
tldr: 该论文首次系统研究了视觉语言模型的道德谄媚现象，发现模型在用户提出异议时，即使初始道德判断正确也常给出错误回应，且表现出从道德正确转向道德错误的单向不对称倾向。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first systematic study of moral sycophancy in vision-language models, revealing that models frequently produce morally incorrect follow-up responses under user disagreement and exhibit a consistent asymmetry toward shifting from morally right to morally wrong judgments.
